narrative.overview:
The surface is paper before it is screen. Everything sits on a warm cream (#FBF4EC) that never goes pure white, text is a soft brown-black (#2A1F16) that never goes pure black, and the one accent is a confident orange used sparingly. The reference is a well-kept personal notebook: warm stock, a confident hand, generous margins, and the occasional mark in the margin.

The system is studious without being clinical. Fraunces gives headlines a literary weight that a geometric sans would flatten into software; Work Sans keeps the reading calm; Space Mono is reserved for the things you handle rather than read.

Warmth here is functional, not decorative. The audience is adults who feel self-conscious about speaking, and the visual world is deliberately unhurried and un-institutional so that using it never feels like sitting an exam.
keyCharacteristics: Paper-warm surfaces; pure white and pure black are absent by design
A single orange accent, plus peach as its quiet form
Serif display / sans body / mono label - three voices, strictly assigned
Flat at rest, lifting only in response to the cursor
Generous vertical air (88px section rhythm) and a 1040px reading column

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Signal Orange is the system's only accent. When something needs emphasis and orange is already spoken for, reach for peach, weight, or space - never for a new hue.

rules.name: The No Pure Rule
rules.body: Nothing is #FFFFFF or #000000. White is #FFFCF8, black is #2A1F16. A pure value anywhere is a bug, not a choice.

rules.name: The Earned Exception Rule
rules.body: Exactly one surface escapes the paper world: the near-black Monero pricing card, whose gravity is the point. A second exception must earn itself the same way. The green supporter medal currently does not, and is a known drift to reconcile.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Fraunces says it, Work Sans explains it, Space Mono labels it. A serif paragraph, a mono sentence, or a sans hero all break the system.

rules.name: The Handled-Value Rule
rules.body: If a value is meant to be copied, counted, or compared, it is Space Mono. If it is meant to be read, it is not.

rules.name: The Reading Column Rule
rules.body: Prose never exceeds ~620px even when its container is wider. The 1040px shell is for layout, not for line length.

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every shadow is rgba(74, 44, 20, ...). A grey or black shadow anywhere in this system is a defect.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Cards, buttons, and chips carry ambient shadow or none. Elevation is earned by hover, focus, or genuine prominence - never assigned decoratively.

rules.name: The Pill-Means-Token Rule
rules.body: border-radius: 100px marks something as a label, count, or code - never a container of prose.

dos: Do keep Signal Orange scarce - roughly one primary action per view.
Do assign the three faces strictly: Fraunces to headline, Work Sans to prose, Space Mono to handled values.
Do convey depth by tone first (Warm Cream, Toasted Cream, Card White) and reach for shadow second.
Do stop looping animation completely under prefers-reduced-motion.
Do design labels to survive Polish, which runs materially longer than Spanish or English.
Do use 100px radius only for tokens (badges, codes, counts, pills).
donts: Don't use a grey or black shadow.
Don't add a fourth typeface, or a new hue outside the orange family, without an exception as earned as the Monero card's.
Don't treat the green supporter medal as a precedent - it is recorded drift, not a sanctioned accent.
Don't make the waveform loop, or animate it on every navigation; it draws once.
Don't put prose inside a pill.
Don't stack more than three tonal layers; there is no fourth surface colour.
